key_insight: Nanoindentation can trigger shear-driven devitrification in amorphous refractory metals, and their crystal forming ability varies strongly across the series, with V transforming most readily and W most resistant.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict when protective amorphous coatings may crystallize under contact loading, guiding refractory alloy selection for harder and more stable surfaces.
method: Melt-quenched amorphous V, Nb, Mo, Ta, and W were prepared and validated against ab initio liquid radial distribution functions.
Large-scale molecular dynamics nanoindentation was used to measure bcc transformation kinetics and local atomic deformation.
A grain population balance framework linked nucleation, growth, and coalescence to the final microstructure.
evidence_signal: The study reports a sigmoidal bcc-fraction-versus-depth response, a CFA ranking of V > Mo > Nb > Ta > W, and a velocity scaling of CFA ∝ v^-m with mean exponent 1.08.
watch_item: The findings come from simulation with specific interatomic potentials and loading conditions, so direct transfer to experiments and different coating chemistries should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Crystal forming ability of amorphous refractory metals under nanoindentation: a molecular dynamics study
